title: Water Drops Skate on a Pan Hotter Than 200 Degrees

scenes.text: A water drop can skate across a pan hotter than boiling without vanishing.
Above about two hundred degrees Celsius, the bottom of the drop flashes into vapor.
That vapor is a terrible heat conductor, about thirty times worse than water.
So the drop floats on its own steam, almost no friction, shielded from the heat.
Colder pan, it boils off in seconds. Hotter pan, it lasts longer.
The hotter it gets, the longer it lives.

description:
Above about 200 degrees Celsius, a drop of water floats on a cushion of its own vapor.
That vapor layer insulates the drop, so it lasts longer on a hotter pan. It is called the Leidenfrost effect.
Have you ever seen water dance on a hot pan?
first_comment: Hot pan, cold water: what happens at your stove?
